families.name: Scope and engagement
families.primary_iep_decision: When the homeowner's expectation, the agreed scope, and the documented work differ, should the program pause scope-dependent criticism and ask for clarification, rather than assume work was omitted?

families.name: Document completeness and integrity
families.primary_iep_decision: When something referenced in the report cannot be found in the supplied file, should the program always treat it as a request for the missing document, never as evidence the work was not done?

families.name: Chronology and condition timing
families.primary_iep_decision: Should every observation and measurement be tied to the date it describes, and should the program refuse to use current-day conditions to confirm or rule out past conditions?

families.name: Moisture measurement interpretation
families.primary_iep_decision: What is the minimum information a moisture reading needs (instrument, mode, material, location, comparison basis) before the program will treat a word like 'elevated' or 'dry' as supported?

families.name: Visual and thermal observations
families.primary_iep_decision: Should a thermal image or visual observation that has not been checked with a contact measurement be treated only as an area for further investigation?

families.name: Moisture source and causation
families.primary_iep_decision: How strongly must the evidence support a stated source before the program accepts 'confirmed' wording instead of asking about 'likely' or 'possible'?

families.name: Sampling purpose, design, and identity
families.primary_iep_decision: Should the program first ask what decision a sample was meant to support, and evaluate sampling only against that stated purpose?

families.name: Laboratory results and interpretation
families.primary_iep_decision: When a conclusion goes further than the laboratory method can support, should the program ask a clarifying question rather than mark the conclusion wrong?

families.name: Recommendations and next steps
families.primary_iep_decision: Should every recommendation be traceable to a specific finding and location, with conditional recommendations clearly labeled as conditional?

families.name: Restoration, remediation, and verification records
families.primary_iep_decision: When a document is a drying record, remediation protocol, or verification report, should the program switch to that document type's expectations instead of assessment-report expectations?

families.name: Commercial and multi-party buildings
families.primary_iep_decision: In shared or commercial buildings, should the program ask about boundaries (suite versus building, shared systems, responsible party) before asking about completeness?

families.name: Homeowner communication quality
families.primary_iep_decision: Should the program show what the report already does well, and rank questions by how much they change the homeowner's decision rather than by how many rules fired?

shared_controls.name: Clarify, do not accuse
shared_controls.text: Every output is a question or a neutral note. No finding of fault, negligence, violation, or failure.

shared_controls.name: Evidence before questions
shared_controls.text: A question is released only with a page-and-location anchor or an explicit evidence state. 'Not located in the supplied documents' never becomes 'not performed'.

shared_controls.name: Scope gate
shared_controls.text: Rules tagged scope-dependent are suppressed until scope is confirmed or documented (IEP-K-001).

shared_controls.name: Privacy and permission
shared_controls.text: Client names, addresses, and report contents stay inside the case. Exports strip identifying data unless explicitly approved.

shared_controls.name: Drafts stay private
shared_controls.text: Nothing reaches a homeowner until a human reviewer approves the exact final artifact. Approval becomes stale if anything changes.

shared_controls.name: Product boundaries
shared_controls.text: No license checks, no legal conclusions, no medical or health advice, no recommendation of specific vendors, no suggestion of additional testing.

shared_controls.name: No outside thresholds
shared_controls.text: The program never inserts a numeric moisture, humidity, spore, drying, or clearance limit that the report itself did not state.

shared_controls.name: Human override recorded
shared_controls.text: Reviewers may approve, rewrite, suppress, merge, or reorder any question; every action records who, when, and a reason code.

entries.title: Separate expectation, agreed scope, and documented work
entries.principle: Treat what the homeowner expected, what the professional agreed to perform, and what the report documents as three separate facts. A gap between them is a clarification opportunity, not a deficiency.
entries.rationale: Homeowners often believe an inspection covered more than was contracted. Treating that belief as the scope produces unfair criticism and undermines trust in the product.
not_applies_to: documents with no scope statement and no agreement where the client also gives no expectation
evidence_required: client intake answer about expected scope
decision_steps: Record each of the three facts with its source.
If agreement is missing and expectation differs from the report scope, set evidence state to 'scope unconfirmed'.
Suppress completeness questions that depend on the disputed scope.
Release one neutral scope-clarification question instead.
exceptions: If the report itself promises work it does not document, a completeness question is allowed because the gap is internal to the report.
prohibited_inferences: Do not state or imply the inspector failed to perform work outside a confirmed scope.
entries.homeowner_question: You expected the inspection to cover [area/service]. The report describes [stated scope]. Could you confirm whether [area/service] was part of the agreed work?
entries.reviewer_action: Check that no scope-dependent question was released before scope was confirmed.
entries.example: Homeowner expected the attic to be checked; the report states the visit was limited to the primary bathroom; no agreement supplied. Program asks one scope question and suppresses attic-related completeness questions.
entries.counterexample: Report scope says 'whole-home visual assessment including attic' but the attic is never mentioned. That is an internal gap; a completeness question is appropriate.
source_hints: Engagement agreement or proposal (ask the homeowner)

entries.title: Classify the document type before reviewing it
entries.principle: Identify whether the document is an assessment, laboratory report, remediation protocol, drying record, verification report, or a mixed package before applying any expectations.
entries.rationale: Each document type answers a different question. Applying assessment expectations to a laboratory report or drying log generates questions the author was never expected to answer.
decision_steps: Classify each document in the package separately.
If classification confidence is low, route to the reviewer before rules run.
Load only rule families tagged for that document type.
exceptions: A mixed package may hold several types; classify per section and keep anchors per section.
prohibited_inferences: Do not treat a laboratory report alone as a building assessment.
entries.reviewer_action: Confirm or correct the document-type classification before release.
entries.example: Package contains a 4-page lab report and a 20-page assessment. Lab-interpretation rules run on the assessment narrative; completeness rules do not run on the lab report.
entries.counterexample: A one-page invoice with a sample list attached is not an assessment report; the program should abstain and ask for the full report.

entries.title: Respect stated limitations and access restrictions
entries.principle: When a report states that an area was not accessed, a material was not opened, or a condition was not evaluated, treat that as documented scope, not as an omission.
entries.rationale: Limitations are a sign of a careful report. Penalizing them would reward reports that hide their boundaries.
decision_steps: Extract each limitation and link it to the areas it covers.
Suppress completeness questions for those areas.
If the homeowner's concern falls inside a limitation, ask whether follow-up is recommended.
exceptions: If a limitation is generic boilerplate that contradicts specific findings in the same area, ask a consistency question.
prohibited_inferences: Do not describe a stated limitation as a failure.
entries.homeowner_question: The report notes that [area] was not accessed. Since your concern involves that area, would you recommend a follow-up evaluation, and what would it involve?
entries.reviewer_action: Make sure limitation-covered areas show 'outside stated scope', not 'missing'.
entries.example: Report states 'wall cavities were not opened.' Homeowner concern is a stain behind the shower. Program asks whether follow-up is recommended.
entries.counterexample: Boilerplate says 'no areas were accessed behind finishes', but page 9 shows a photo of an opened cavity with readings. Ask which statement applies.
source_hints: ASTM D7338-26 reporting and limitation language (licensed)
entries.iep_question: Should generic boilerplate limitations count as scope, or only limitations tied to a specific area?

entries.title: Identify the engagement objective
entries.principle: Determine what question the professional was hired to answer (for example: is there hidden moisture, what is the source, is remediation complete) and evaluate the report against that objective.
entries.rationale: A report can be thorough and still not answer the question the client needed answered. Conversely, it should not be judged against questions it was never asked.
decision_steps: Extract the stated objective.
Compare to the client's stated reason.
If the report's conclusions do not address its own objective, raise one question.
If no objective is stated, set 'objective not stated' and ask once.
exceptions: Real-estate transaction inspections may have a narrower objective set by the buyer's agreement.
prohibited_inferences: Do not assume the objective from the homeowner's worry alone.
entries.homeowner_question: The report's stated purpose is [objective]. Does its conclusion answer that question, or is further work needed to answer it?
entries.reviewer_action: Check that questions are tied to the stated objective, not to the homeowner's broader worries.
entries.example: Purpose: 'determine source of ceiling stain.' Conclusions discuss air samples but never name a source. Ask whether the source was identified.
entries.counterexample: Purpose: 'collect air samples at client request.' No source discussion is expected; no source question.
entries.iep_question: Which objectives do you see most often, so the program can offer them as a fixed list?

entries.title: Current readings do not describe past conditions
entries.principle: A reading taken on the inspection date describes that date. It should not be used by itself to confirm or rule out a past moisture event.
entries.rationale: Materials can dry after a leak while damage or growth remains. Homeowners often read 'dry' as 'nothing happened'.
not_applies_to: drying records whose purpose is current condition
decision_steps: Identify historical-event statements.
Identify current readings used to address them.
If the report uses current dry readings to dismiss a past event, ask a chronology question.
exceptions: If the report explicitly distinguishes current from historical conditions, suppress.
prohibited_inferences: Do not state that damage exists because a past event occurred.
entries.homeowner_question: Does this reading describe conditions on the inspection date only, and does the report address whether the earlier water event caused damage that is still present?
entries.reviewer_action: Make sure the question does not suggest hidden damage exists.
entries.example: Client reports a dishwasher leak 4 months ago. Report: 'cabinet base reads dry; no concerns.' Chronology question.
